title: Reuters Institute: Digital News Report 2026 landing page
answer: This is the Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism landing page for its Digital News Report 2026. It offers a podcast series about the report and a topic index. The most useful thing it shows for AI in media is that AI and journalism is a listed topic and that one podcast episode is titled AI and the future of news. The page itself gives no findings, figures, or methodology.

sections.body: The source is a page on the Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism website. It is the landing page for the Digital News Report 2026. The page presents a podcast series about the report and a search by topic menu. The title states the year 2026. The text does not describe the report's survey scope, markets, methodology, or publication date beyond the year in the title.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page says, Our podcast series, and invites listeners to hear episodes on the report. It names seven episodes: Key findings, News creators, Why traditional news organisations are losing audiences, AI and the future of news, The rise of news video, Attitudes towards impartiality, and Social benefits of public service news. The page also offers a Search by topic menu. The topics listed include AI and journalism, Audience Engagement, Business of news, Climate journalism, Conflict Reporting, COVID-19, Data Journalism, Foreign correspondence, Investigative Journalism, Israel-Gaza war, Journalism and elections, Journalism beats, Journalism in exile, Journalists at work, Local News, Media regulation, Mental Health, Misinformation, News Avoidance, News creators, News podcasts, Newsroom Diversity, Newsroom Leadership, OSINT, Platforms and social media, Polarisation, Press Freedom, Public Service Media, Solutions Journalism, Trust In News, War in Ukraine, and Workplace conditions. Beyond these labels, the page does not summarise any report content. It does not state what the report found about AI, trust, newsroom adoption, or audience behaviour. It does not give figures, charts, country names, sample sizes, or dates for the report's release. The only AI-specific items visible are the topic AI and journalism and the podcast episode AI and the future of news.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source gives no figures, statistics, or numerical findings. It lists seven podcast episodes, numbered 1 to 7, and a set of topic labels. The only AI-related labels are AI and journalism and AI and the future of news. No other numerical findings or definitions appear in the text.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in media would use this page mainly as a pointer. It confirms that the Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2026 treats AI and journalism as a topic and that its podcast series includes an episode called AI and the future of news. The page does not itself supply audience data, trust measures, or newsroom adoption evidence. To get substance on AI in news, a reader would need to follow the linked report or podcast, which this landing page does not reproduce.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Media

sections.body: The page is a partial landing page, not the report. It does not cover findings, methodology, market list, sample sizes, or publication date beyond 2026. It does not explain what AI and journalism means in the report or what the AI podcast episode concludes. It is published by the Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism and is navigational rather than a full research document. The text does not state that the report is survey-based or published in full.
